question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{16}({x}^{2}-y),\, & 0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{5}{3},$ $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{20}{21},$ and $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]=\frac{40}{27},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2},
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

First, we find $\text{Var}[X].$
We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}\frac{5}{16}{x}^{2}({x}^{2}-y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}({x}^{4}-y{x}^{2})\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}{[y{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}{x}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y={x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{6})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{32}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{6}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{32}{[\frac{1}{7}{x}^{7}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{20}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{20}{7}-{(\frac{5}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{63}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we compute $\text{Var}[Y].$ Using the given results, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =\frac{40}{27}-{(\frac{20}{21})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{760}{1\,323}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's find $\text{Cov}[X,Y].$ By the rule of the lazy statistician, we find $\text{E}[XY]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}xy\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}\frac{5}{16}xy({x}^{2}-y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}({x}^{3}y-x{y}^{2})\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}x]}_{y=0}^{y={x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{1}{6}{x}^{7})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{96}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{7}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{96}{[\frac{1}{8}{x}^{8}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{5}{3}-(\frac{5}{3})\cdot (\frac{20}{21}) \\  & =\frac{5}{63}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{63} & \frac{5}{63} \\ \frac{5}{63} & \frac{760}{1\,323}\end{aligned}].
$$
